question: slides Theory/Deadlock problem.pdf
source: Teacher's notes, BCSE303L Module 3 (CPU scheduling & deadlocks)
text: Four processes P0–P3, resources R1 (2), R2 (3), R3, R4 (2). R1: one each to P0, P1. R2: one each to P1, P2, P3. R3: two allocated to P0, one free. R4: one each to P3, P2. Requests: P1 → 1 R1; P0 → 1 R2; P3 → 1 R1 + 2 R2; P0 and P2 → 1 R3 each. Draw the resource-allocation graph, apply the Banker's (detection) algorithm, and give the safe sequence if there is no deadlock.
notes: No answer key in the notes. Engine: no deadlock; P2 → P0 → P1 → P3. (Read as R3 having 3 instances; if R3 has 2 with one held by P0, Available is the same and so is the answer.)
